problems.title: Find the Town Judge
problems.notes: in-degree/out-degree counting — a graph problem disguised as trivia; the judge has indegree n-1 and outdegree 0

problems.title: Island Perimeter
problems.notes: simple grid DFS/BFS, or count edges directly: 4 per land cell minus 2 per land-land adjacency

problems.title: Is Graph Bipartite?
problems.notes: 2-color via BFS/DFS; a graph is bipartite iff it has no odd-length cycle, which coloring detects directly

problems.title: Keys and Rooms
problems.notes: pure reachability DFS/BFS from room 0 — can every node be visited from the start?

problems.title: Reorder Routes to Make All Paths Lead to the City Zero
problems.notes: DFS from city 0 on the undirected view of the graph, counting edges that point the 'wrong' way (away from 0)

problems.title: Flower Planting With No Adjacent
problems.notes: graph coloring with only 4 colors needed, since every node has at most 3 neighbors by the problem's constraints

problems.title: Shortest Path with Alternating Colors
problems.notes: BFS over an augmented (node, lastEdgeColor) state space — plain BFS on the node graph alone loses the alternation constraint

problems.title: Number of Squareful Arrays
problems.notes: model valid adjacent pairs (sum is a perfect square) as graph edges, then Hamiltonian-path-style backtracking over permutations
